tasks.short: Write a care plan with the social worker and the client.

steps.what: Read the client file before meeting clients
Meet clients and watch how they are coping
Develop the care plans with the social worker
Type the agreed care plan into the client file
Sign the care plan version just written
Implement the signed plans with the client

tasks.design: She reads the open client file in {OTHER}, meets the client, and develops the plan with the social worker. She types that agreed plan into {OTHER} herself, and the social worker signs that version before she carries it out with the client. No model sets the goals.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan is a judgement about this client. A blank form does not watch the meeting or choose the goals.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new writes the plan. One signed copy in the client file is enough, and she still types every goal.
tasks.still_hard: Thin notes and a client who changes their mind still need the meeting. The signature does not make the thinking faster.
tasks.human_edge: She and the social worker stay accountable for the goals. A model must not set them.
tasks.altitude: Her week on this task does not change. She still meets the client, still writes the plan, and still waits for the social worker before she carries it out.

reach.learn: Which goals the social worker will sign, and which an assistant must not put in the file alone.

evidence.claim: Listening to the client, agreeing the goals, and typing the plan stay her time. A form does not shorten that work. Model knowledge.
The client file holds health data, which is a special category and needs a lawful basis and access control.
A decision about a person must not rest solely on automated processing, so the care plan stays with the assistant and the social worker.
A published check of social-work notes found invented content, including risk statements the worker had not recorded, so this plan stays text they write.

assumptions: Listening, developing the plan, typing it, and carrying it out stay at remaining 100. No mechanism shortens those steps.
The assistant types the care plan text. The social worker, another role, signs that stored text before she carries it out. No model sets goals.
Zero extra hours: no new system and no recording of the meeting. A missing signature means she does not carry the plan out, which is the current rule.
The client file is the system she already uses. This task adds no structured field for a machine to consume.
unknowns: Whether this employer requires a social worker signature before every plan is carried out, or only for some plans.
research_questions: Which care plans does this employer require a social worker to sign before the assistant acts?

already_counted.description: Reading the file, meeting the client, developing the plan, typing it, and carrying it out are already her remaining time on those steps.
The social worker's signature is already that other role's time on the sign step, not her saving.

incremental.description: No extra steady hours. There is no new tool to keep, and a missing signature is the existing stop, not a new task.

approvals.approved_version: Care plan text typed into the client file and signed by the social worker before she carries it out.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step of hers is shorter. The meeting, the goals, the typing, and carrying the plan out stay at full length. A missing signature stops implementation, which is the current rule, not a time cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record client visits and drop the second tally.

steps.what: Keep records of visits with clients
Retype visit counts onto the management sheet
Mail that management sheet to the owner

tasks.design: She types visit date, client id, service, and the note into the {OTHER} client file at full length; she is the producer of those fields. A filter on that same record replaces the second typing into the {SPREADSHEET} and the {EMAIL} of that sheet to the owner. If any of those fields is missing, she still retypes and still mails, and this saving does not apply.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visit notes were free text, so a count for the owner meant reading them again and retyping.
tasks.enabler_now: Visit date, client id, service, and the note, typed once by her in the client file, can be filtered without a second sheet.
tasks.still_hard: Writing what happened on the visit stays hers. A missing field means the old retype returns.
tasks.human_edge: She does not file a visit she did not record. The owner sees counts, not a judgement about the client.
tasks.altitude: She still writes each visit record at full length. She stops retyping the same fields for the owner only when those fields are already in the file.

reach.task: Prepare activity reports for a supervisor.
reach.learn: Which visit fields are already stored so a second tally is not retyped.

evidence.claim: Filtering fields she already typed removes only the second tally and its mail. It does not shorten writing the visit. Model knowledge.
Visit notes about a client are special-category data, so a manager's view of them still needs a lawful basis and access control.

assumptions: Structured fields are visit date, client id, service, and the note. The producer is the assistant in the record step, and that capture stays at remaining 100. The retype and the mail only copy those fields.
If the client file does not store those fields, she still retypes and still mails, and the saving does not apply. There is no extraction step that invents them.
Zero extra hours for her: the filter is not her labour, and she does not keep a second workbook. The owner's reading of the same file is not moved onto her hours.
Keeping the visit record stays at remaining 100. Only the second copy and its mail are removed, and only by that filter.
unknowns: Whether visit date, client id, service, and the note are stored as separate fields today, or only inside free text.
research_questions: Does the client file already store visit date, client id, service, and the note as fields the owner can open?

already_counted.description: Writing the visit record, including visit date, client id, service, and the note, is already her remaining time on the record step.

incremental.description: No extra steady hours. A missing field means she keeps the retype, so the saving does not apply, rather than a new upkeep task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The retype is 8 percent and the mail is 6 percent, and both drop only when she already stored visit date, client id, service, and the note. Low keeps the mail when the owner cannot open the file. High drops both and leaves a little when some owners still ask for a copy.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain agency services on a home or group visit.

steps.what: Arrange the home visit with the person
Find agency services and requirements to explain
Visit the home or attend the group meeting

tasks.design: The team lead keeps a service list in {DOCS}, indexed by agency name, with the fields service name, requirement, and procedure, and updates it when a service changes. She still reads the matching row, and when the row is missing she searches the old pack inside that same step. The home visit, the group meeting, and what she tells the person stay at full length.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service rules sat in old packs, and the right sheet was hard to find before the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: A list the team lead updates, indexed by agency name, removes that search. She still reads the row.
tasks.still_hard: The list does not know which service this household needs. A missing row sends her back to the pack.
tasks.human_edge: She tells the person in the room. The list does not decide eligibility.
tasks.altitude: She still makes the visit and still explains the service. She spends less time hunting for the sheet only when the row exists.

reach.task: Confer with clients to discuss their options and goals.
reach.learn: Which agency requirement she must say aloud, and which the list must not decide.

evidence.claim: An indexed list shortens the search for a service sheet. It does not shorten the home visit or the group meeting. Model knowledge.
A decision about a person must not rest solely on automated processing, so she still explains the service and does not let a rule decide eligibility.
Eligibility for public assistance by or for a public authority is a high-risk use, so this design does not score who qualifies.

assumptions: Service-list fields are agency name, service name, requirement, and procedure. The producer is the team lead when a service changes. Her capture is reading the row inside the find step, which stays at remaining 70.
A missing row: she searches the old pack inside that same step, and the shorter time does not apply. Nothing extracts a requirement she did not read.
The team lead's upkeep is about one hour per 100 of her baseline hours on this task. That is another role and is not taken off her saving.
Zero extra hours for her, because a missing row is already inside the find step. Arranging the visit and telling the person stay at remaining 100.
The list quotes a service. It does not say the household qualifies.
unknowns: Whether a team lead already keeps an agency list, and how often a service changes.
research_questions: Who updates agency name, service name, requirement, and procedure today, and how often?

already_counted.description: Arranging the visit, reading the service row, and making the visit are already her remaining time on those steps.

incremental.description: No extra steady hours for her. A missing row is handled inside the find step, and she does not maintain the list.
The team lead updates agency name, service name, requirement, and procedure when a service changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the find step changes, and only because the team lead's list is indexed by agency name. She still reads the row. Low is when many rows are missing and she opens the old pack. High is when most rows exist. The home visit and the group meeting stay at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review client problems with her superior.

steps.what: Read the reports she will review
Mail those reports to her superior
Review reports and problems with her superior

tasks.design: She reads the visit record already stored in the {OTHER} client file, which she produced earlier with visit date, client id, service, and the note. The second {EMAIL} of that report drops only when the superior can open the same file; otherwise she still mails it. The review of problems with her superior stays a full meeting, and no model rewrites the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: The superior did not always open the client file, so she mailed a second copy of reports she had already written.
tasks.enabler_now: When the superior can open the same file, that mail is the same report, not a new one.
tasks.still_hard: The review is a conversation. A mail does not settle a problem with a client.
tasks.human_edge: She and the superior judge the problems. No model rewrites the report they discuss.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the reports and still sits the review at full length. The extra mail drops only when the superior already has the file.

reach.role: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
reach.task: Review client problems with a supervisor.
reach.learn: Which problems the superior still wants to hear in the meeting, rather than from a mailed copy.

evidence.claim: Opening the same stored report removes a second mail. It does not shorten the review meeting. Model knowledge.
A published check of social-work notes found invented content, including risk statements the worker had not recorded, so the report they discuss stays the text she wrote.
The client file holds health data, which is a special category, so the superior's access still needs a lawful basis.
In the Netherlands, recording staff conversations needs works-council consent. This design does not record her. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The report the mail would send is the visit record she already wrote: visit date, client id, service, and the note. The producer is the assistant on the records task, where that capture stays at full length. Here she reads it again at remaining 100.
The second mail drops only when the superior can open the same client file. Otherwise she still mails it, and the saving does not apply. Nothing extracts a report she did not write.
Zero extra hours: no recording of the review and no second store. Works-council consent for recording staff is not triggered because she is not recorded.
Reading the reports and the review with her superior stay at remaining 100. Only the duplicate mail is removed, and only by that shared file.
unknowns: Whether the superior can already open the client file without a mailed copy.
research_questions: Does the superior already have access to the visit record she stored, or only to what she mails?

already_counted.description: Reading the stored reports and reviewing problems with her superior are already her remaining time on those steps.

incremental.description: No extra steady hours. If the superior cannot open the file she still mails the report, so the saving does not apply.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The only cut is the second mail, 8 percent, of a report she already stored. Low is zero when the superior cannot open the file and she still mails it. High is 6 when most superiors open the file and a few still want a copy. The review stays at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week stays with clients and the superior. A visit count does not write the care plan, does not tell a household what they are eligible for, and does not replace the review meeting.
reach: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
skills_to_grow: Write the plan herself when notes are thin.
Do not file a visit count she did not record.
Leave eligibility and the superior's review as human.
role.ambitious_version: One visit record feeds the management tally, while the care plan, the home visit, and the review stay in her hands.
